svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
Juice Shop · 8 components · 20 data flows · 7 trust boundaries (1 inferred) · 55 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-03; tb-2 External → C-08; tb-4 External → C-07; tb-6 C-03 → External; tb-8 C-07 → External
Trust boundary crossing: tb-5 C-01 → C-06
df-001: Server-side fetch of a requester-supplied profile image URL (HTTP)
df-002: Challenge-solved notification with solution, CTF flag and host details (HTTP)
df-003: Startup probe of the LLM model list (HTTP) df-004: Chatbot requests via an OpenAI-compatible provider client carrying an API key (HTTP)
df-005: Ethereum contract event subscriptions through an Alchemy WebSocket provider (WebSocket)
df-006: Profile image update through the user model · Sequelize (in-process)

df-007: ORM reads and writes to the SQLite file · SQLite (embedded) df-007 authentication: Embedded SQLite engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-009: OAuth authorization (HTTPS) df-009 authentication: The identity provider authenticates the user at its sign-in endpoint; evidence: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:31, frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148
df-010: OAuth profile request (HTTPS) df-010 authentication: The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/user.service.ts:68

df-011: API requests (bearer) (HTTP) df-011 authentication: the handler checks a bearer credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:178, lib/insecurity.ts:52, routes/orderHistory.ts:13, lib/insecurity.ts:156
df-012: API requests (unknown authentication) (HTTP) df-013: API requests (unknown authentication) (HTTP)

df-015: API requests (bearer) (HTTP) df-015 authentication: the handler checks a bearer credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:178, lib/insecurity.ts:52 df-015 access group: API access; alternatives; step n/a

df-016: API requests (other) (HTTP) df-016 authentication: the handler checks the supplied TOTP code against the account secret and rejects an invalid code; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:31 df-016 access group: API access; alternatives; step n/a

df-017: API requests (password) (HTTP) df-017 authentication: the handler checks the supplied password and rejects the request without a valid one; evidence: routes/login.ts:34 df-017 access group: API access; alternatives; step n/a

df-019: Direct requests (cookie) (HTTP) df-019 authentication: the handler checks a cookie credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: routes/profileImageFileUpload.ts:35, routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:21, routes/userProfile.ts:34, routes/updateUserProfile.ts:17, routes/dataErasure.ts:26, routes/dataErasure.ts:76

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
trust change within a column (dashed: inferred)
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE category: filled = findings in that category
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
